transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How have things been since we spoke on the phone?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Up and down. More down, if I'm honest. It's been about two months now of feeling flat.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Flat in what way?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Like the colour's gone out of things. I used to love my pottery class and I've skipped the last four.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is that because you don't enjoy it any more, or for another reason?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Partly I don't enjoy it. Partly the class moved to Thursday evenings and that clashes with my shift. So it's a bit of both.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How would you rate your mood from zero to ten, where ten is the best you've felt?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Today maybe a four. On a bad day a two. I had one good weekend last month where it was a seven.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How many bad days in a typical week?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Two, maybe three. The rest are just sort of grey.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you find yourself crying more than usual?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: A little. Mostly in the car on the way home.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or of harming yourself?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No. Nothing like that. I've got my kids, and I wouldn't.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Any feelings of guilt, or of being worthless?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Guilt, yes. I feel like I'm letting the kids down when I'm too tired to play with them. Worthless, no, I wouldn't say that.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How's your concentration?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Worse. I reread the same paragraph at work. My supervisor hasn't said anything, though.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Let's talk about worry. Do you find yourself worrying a lot?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: All the time. Money, the kids, whether I'm doing my job right. It's like a constant hum in the background.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is it hard to stop once it starts?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Very. Especially at night.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How long has the worry been like this?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Honestly, years. I've always been a worrier, my mum was the same. It just feels louder since the mood dipped.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you ever had a panic attack, where your heart races and you feel you can't breathe?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Not a full one, no. My chest has gone tight in the supermarket queue, but it passed after a minute and I didn't feel like I was dying or anything.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How often does the chest tightness happen?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Maybe twice in the last month.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you avoid places because of it?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Avoid them? I don't know. I still do the shopping.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you go at different times, or to a different shop?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I go early on a Sunday now, when it's quieter. I suppose that's a kind of avoiding.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Any physical symptoms with the worry, like muscle tension or stomach upsets?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: My shoulders are always up by my ears. And headaches, a few a week.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you seen your GP about the headaches?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Not yet. I've been meaning to.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Now, sleep. How are you sleeping?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Badly. I fall asleep fine around eleven, but I wake at four and can't get back off.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How many nights a week?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Most nights. Five, maybe.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you nap during the day to make up for it?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Do I nap? Hmm, it depends what you call a nap.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: And what about your appetite?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Down. I skip breakfast and I'm picking at dinner.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has your weight changed?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: My jeans are looser. I haven't weighed myself, though.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What about alcohol?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: A glass of wine most evenings, to take the edge off. Two on a Friday.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has that increased recently?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: A bit. It used to be just weekends.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What has helped, if anything?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Walking the dog. When I actually get out, I feel a bit better for an hour or so.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you had a period like this before?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: After my second child was born I had a few months like this. I saw a counsellor then and it helped.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Would you be open to talking therapy again?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Yes, I think I would. I just need it to fit around my shifts.

assessment.label: Mood
assessment.text: Reports approximately two months of persistently low mood, rating it four out of ten today, with two to three bad days per week. Has stopped attending a pottery class due to loss of enjoyment. Endorses feelings of guilt and worthlessness. Denies suicidal thoughts or thoughts of self-harm. A similar episode followed the birth of her second child and responded to counselling.

assessment.label: Anxiety
assessment.text: Describes long-standing, pervasive worry about finances, her children and work, which has intensified alongside the low mood. Experiences panic attacks in the supermarket several times a week. Avoids shopping entirely. Reports daily headaches.

assessment.label: Sleep and appetite
assessment.text: Early-morning waking around four on most nights, with no difficulty falling asleep. Compensates for lost sleep with daytime naps. Reduced appetite with documented weight loss. Drinks two glasses of wine every night.
